response: {"title":"Nearest-boundary counterexample requirement","intervention":"For every behavior-changing edit, construct and run one nearest-valid and one nearest-invalid counterexample at the edited branch, asserting the exact value or the exact exception class and message before considering that edit complete.","claim":"Against no appended instruction on matched Python repair tasks, this instruction will raise held-out boundary and invalid-input pass_rate under the same deadline, with wall_time and turns tracked for overhead.","mechanism":"Pairing adjacent valid and invalid witnesses forces the agent to locate the true contract boundary and distinguishes an intended rejection from an off-by-one condition, overly broad exception, or message mismatch at the moment each branch is changed.","assumptions":["Edited branches admit concrete adjacent valid and invalid inputs.","Exact expected outcomes can be derived from specifications, tests, callers, or stable repository conventions.","Focused examples can be executed within the fixed deadline."],"risks":["Some domains lack a natural nearest input, causing arbitrary examples.","Locally correct counterexamples may miss cross-module interactions or stateful sequences.","Deriving an exact message from ambiguous evidence can encode the wrong contract.","Running two witnesses per edit may consume time needed for broader fixes."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks between this appended instruction and no appended instruction using identical models, tools, and deadlines; evaluate with hidden tests stratified by boundary values, malformed and wrong-type inputs, exception class, and exact message.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm achieves higher hidden pass_rate overall and on the edge-semantics stratum while staying within the deadline and without a material increase in median turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":2}
